newsitem.title: New Zealand: NZ shares edge down at close, rally cools off.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares edge down at close, rally cools off.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices edged down slightly
* Effect of last week's rally flows on to second tier
* Transport stocks gain. Mainfreight at post-float high
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
328 +1 * NZSC cap index +22.77 at 4,440.40
380 nil * Volume NZ$46.3 million. Futures -5 at 1,123
685 -5 * Other movers - +4 +12
New Zealand's share market cooled a little on Monday, but second tier stocks did benefit from a flow-on effect after last week's rally.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index was down 2.62 points at 2,219.97, mostly due to Telecom edging back five to NZ$6.85. Most other leaders were steady-to-mixed.
The second tier enjoyed a renaissance, the smaller companies index gaining 22.77 points to 4,440.40. Overall, profit-taking had been partly offset by unsatisfied demand from last week.
While there had been slight weakness in the session, Luke Koekoek at JB Were doubted the market had too much downside.
Conversely, the proximity of the Octber 12 election would probably be a disincentive for the market to race away.
Koekoek said the market was underpinned by offshore demand.

Freight forwarder Mainfreight gained one cent to NZ$1.10 -- its highest point since listing in June and a 14-cent premium to its NZ$0.96 issue price. Trucking and shipping company Owens gained four to NZ$1.94.
Port of Tauranga was pumped up 12 cents to NZ$1.92 after a better-than-expected annual result.
Force attracted big turnover when interests associated with chairman Peter Francis sold 6.5 million shares at NZ$0.76 a share, the stock closing unchanged at NZ$0.74.
In gold, Macraes rose 15 to NZ$3.80, another closing high, and Otter Gold firmed nine to $2.10.
The market now was awaiting annual results from Fletcher Challenge on Wednesday and Air New Zealand next week.
